text:
ConocoPhillips rose 0.5% today to close at $146, continuing a strong two-week rally that has pushed the stock up 12.9%. The gain comes amid a sharp spike in global oil prices — Brent crude topped $109 per barrel on October 19th after Iran-backed Houthi militants attacked Saudi Arabian airports and oil facilities, triggering missile and drone strikes that rattled supply concerns. Though crude slipped slightly today as traders began hoping for diplomatic progress in the Middle East conflict, the price remains elevated, and oil refiners and producers like ConocoPhillips benefit directly when crude costs more.

The stock's two-week surge reflects a broader energy sector rally tied to Middle East geopolitical risk. With the Strait of Hormuz — a critical chokepoint for global oil shipments — now facing escalating attacks on commercial vessels, the market has repriced energy stocks upward on supply-disruption fears. This tug-of-war between rising prices (good for producers' profits) and eventual peace hopes (which would lower prices again) is likely to keep energy stocks volatile in the near term.
